Parse and evaluate simple arithmetic word problems, left to right.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/wordy) (MIT). Listed under [Parsing & Validation](/examples/?subject=parsing-and-validation).

```nomi-run
// FILE: wordy.nomi
/// Why a question has no answer.
pub enum Error {
    UnknownOperation
    SyntaxError
    DivisionByZero
}

/// Answers a word problem such as `What is 3 plus 2 multiplied by 3?`,
/// working left to right with no operator precedence.
pub fn answer(question: String) -> Result<Int, Error> {
    Some(problem) =
        question
        |> String.strip_prefix("What is")
        |> Maybe.flat_map(&String.strip_suffix(&1, "?"))
    else {
        return Err(.UnknownOperation)
    }

    [first, ..rest] = String.words(problem) else {
        return Err(.SyntaxError)
    }
    Some(total) = String.to_int(first) else {
        return Err(.SyntaxError)
    }
    evaluate(total, rest)
}

enum Operation {
    Plus
    Minus
    Times
    DividedBy
}

/// Applies each operation in `words` to the running total in turn.
fn evaluate(total: Int, words: List<String>) -> Result<Int, Error> {
    case words {
        [] -> Ok(total)
        ["plus", ..rest] -> operand(total, .Plus, rest)
        ["minus", ..rest] -> operand(total, .Minus, rest)
        ["multiplied", "by", ..rest] -> operand(total, .Times, rest)
        ["divided", "by", ..rest] -> operand(total, .DividedBy, rest)
        [word, .._] when String.to_int(word) |> Maybe.some?() -> Err(.SyntaxError)
        _ -> Err(.UnknownOperation)
    }
}

/// Reads the number after an operation, applies it and carries on.
fn operand(total: Int, operation: Operation, words: List<String>) -> Result<Int, Error> {
    [word, ..rest] = words else {
        return Err(.SyntaxError)
    }
    Some(n) = String.to_int(word) else {
        return Err(.SyntaxError)
    }
    total = try apply(operation, total, n)
    evaluate(total, rest)
}

fn apply(operation: Operation, a: Int, b: Int) -> Result<Int, Error> {
    case operation {
        .Plus -> Ok(a + b)
        .Minus -> Ok(a - b)
        .Times -> Ok(a * b)
        .DividedBy -> divide(a, b)
    }
}

fn divide(a: Int, b: Int) -> Result<Int, Error> {
    Int.to_non_zero(b) |> Maybe.map(&Int.divide(a, &1)) |> Maybe.to_result(Error.DivisionByZero)
}

// FILE: wordy_test.nomi
import {
    wordy
    wordy.Error
}

test "answers word problems" {
    cases: List<#(String, String, Result<Int, Error>)> = [
        #("just a number", "What is 5?", Ok(5)),
        #("just a zero", "What is 0?", Ok(0)),
        #("just a negative number", "What is -123?", Ok(-123)),
        #("addition", "What is 1 plus 1?", Ok(2)),
        #("addition with a left hand zero", "What is 0 plus 2?", Ok(2)),
        #("addition with a right hand zero", "What is 3 plus 0?", Ok(3)),
        #("more addition", "What is 53 plus 2?", Ok(55)),
        #("addition with negative numbers", "What is -1 plus -10?", Ok(-11)),
        #("large addition", "What is 123 plus 45678?", Ok(45801)),
        #("subtraction", "What is 4 minus -12?", Ok(16)),
        #("multiplication", "What is -3 multiplied by 25?", Ok(-75)),
        #("division", "What is 33 divided by -3?", Ok(-11)),
        #("multiple additions", "What is 1 plus 1 plus 1?", Ok(3)),
        #("addition and subtraction", "What is 1 plus 5 minus -2?", Ok(8)),
        #("multiple subtraction", "What is 20 minus 4 minus 13?", Ok(3)),
        #("subtraction then addition", "What is 17 minus 6 plus 3?", Ok(14)),
        #("multiple multiplication", "What is 2 multiplied by -2 multiplied by 3?", Ok(-12)),
        #("addition and multiplication", "What is -3 plus 7 multiplied by -2?", Ok(-8)),
        #("multiple division", "What is -12 divided by 2 divided by -3?", Ok(2)),
        #("unknown operation", "What is 52 cubed?", Err(.UnknownOperation)),
        #(
            "Non math question",
            "Who is the President of the United States?",
            Err(.UnknownOperation),
        ),
        #("reject problem missing an operand", "What is 1 plus?", Err(.SyntaxError)),
        #("reject problem with no operands or operators", "What is?", Err(.SyntaxError)),
        #("reject two operations in a row", "What is 1 plus plus 2?", Err(.SyntaxError)),
        #("reject two numbers in a row", "What is 1 plus 2 1?", Err(.SyntaxError)),
        #("reject postfix notation", "What is 1 2 plus?", Err(.SyntaxError)),
        #("reject prefix notation", "What is plus 1 2?", Err(.SyntaxError)),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, question, expected), description {
        assert wordy.answer(question) == expected
    }
}

// Not a canonical case: the exercise leaves division by zero open.
test "division by zero" {
    assert wordy.answer("What is 1 divided by 0?") == Err(.DivisionByZero)
}
```

## How it's written

- The evaluator walks the word list with list patterns, including two-word operators (`["multiplied", "by", ..rest]`), instead of tokenizing first.
- Operators are a private `Operation` enum applied by `apply`, rather than lambdas passed around.
- Errors are an `Error` enum. A number where an operator belongs is a syntax error and any other word is an unknown operation, which is the distinction the canonical cases draw.
- Division by zero is `Error.DivisionByZero`, through `Int.to_non_zero` and `Int.divide`, instead of the trap `/` raises. The canonical data has no such case; the test file adds one, marked as not canonical.
- Division is its own `divide` function, one pipe: `Int.to_non_zero(b) |> Maybe.map(&Int.divide(a, &1)) |> Maybe.to_result(Error.DivisionByZero)`. The missing divisor is never bound for later lines, so `Maybe.to_result` as a pipe stage fits rather than a binding `else` (style §16). The capture's open operand takes `NonZeroInt` from the pipe, which picks `Int`'s `Divide<NonZeroInt, Int>` impl. Keeping it out of `apply` keeps each arm there on one line.
- Guards use binding `else` (`[first, ..rest] = String.words(problem) else { ... }`) so the success path stays unindented. The style guide uses a binding `else`, not `Maybe.to_result` with `try`, when the value is bound for the lines that follow, as every guard here is.
- The 27 canonical cases are one `subtests` table.
- The trailing `?` comes off through `Maybe.flat_map(&String.strip_suffix(&1, "?"))`: one call that uses its parameter once, so it is a capture rather than `fn rest -> ...` (style §31).
